record_identity.title: Taiwan reported an AI-assisted cyber campaign against government agencies

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: Reuters reports Taiwan’s Ministry of Digital Affairs confirmed AI-assisted attacks from overseas sources; private firm Dream separately reported multi-agent credential theft and data exfiltration. The government statement did not attribute the attack to China.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: Taiwanese government agencies and connected systems targeted during the reported July 1–4 campaign; Dream reports 85 compromised employee accounts, 2,564+ exfiltrated personnel records and expansion toward additional government and energy-sector targets.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: For the occurrence recorded as ‘Taiwan reported an AI-assisted cyber campaign against government agencies’, the security and operational harm was substantial, but the preserved evidence does not establish the exceptional scale, permanence or gravity required for S1. The evidence does not establish complete duration or reversibility beyond the consequence described.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: Dream reports 12 attack waves over approximately four days, up to eight parallel sub-agents per wave, 85 compromised employee accounts and more than 2,564 exfiltrated personnel records. Taiwan's government confirmation does not independently enumerate all of these figures.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: Taiwan confirmed an AI-assisted attack but not every private-firm quantitative or technical claim. Human operators selected campaign objectives, and autonomous strategic target selection is not established.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S2 rather than S1 is appropriate because the occurrence recorded as ‘Taiwan reported an AI-assisted cyber campaign against government agencies’ is not shown to have caused exceptionally large, permanent or comparably grave harm; S2 rather than S3 is appropriate because the realised security and operational harm was substantial, not merely moderate or incidental.

assessment_boundaries: Taiwan's government confirmation establishes an AI-assisted attack but does not independently verify every quantitative or technical detail reported by Dream Security.
The reviewed evidence does not establish that the agent frameworks autonomously selected the campaign's strategic objectives; human operators initiated and directed the hostile operation.
VIGIL does not attribute the campaign to a state or named threat actor beyond the public evidence.
Malicious use of an agent framework does not by itself establish a selectable VIGIL Failure Class in the framework.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters reports that Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs confirmed AI-assisted attacks against government agencies from overseas sources. Dream Security separately published a technical reconstruction of the July 1–4 campaign based on recovered artefacts, identifying Hermes and OpenClaw as the agent frameworks and reporting 12 attack waves, up to eight parallel sub-agents, 85 compromised employee accounts and exfiltration of more than 2,564 personnel records. VIGIL preserves the government's confirmation separately from Dream's more detailed technical claims.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates operational use of open-source autonomous-agent frameworks in a real government intrusion, with parallelised credential attacks, adaptive targeting and data exfiltration. The hostile operator intentionally supplied the objectives, so VIGIL does not infer that malicious use by itself constitutes an internal governance failure of Hermes or OpenClaw.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: For CAM, the occurrence is a material ecosystem case of agentic cyber capability moving from evaluation and hypothetical misuse into a bounded real-world government intrusion. It highlights governance requirements for agent permissions, unattended execution, attack-surface exposure, model/tool misuse controls and downstream defensive observability.
